newsitem.title: USA: Gillette has no plans for cash from Duracell.
newsitem.headline: Gillette has no plans for cash from Duracell.

text.p: Gillette Co Chief Executive Officer Alfred Zeien said the company has as yet no plans for the cash that will be generated by the combined Gillette/ Duracell International Inc.

"What we do with that cash will be a question before the board of directors," Zeien told the investors in a conference call. He estimated that by 1999, Gillette would have "cash on the balance sheet of $2.6 billion."
Gillette does not plan any major share buybacks, but it might reinstitute its small buyback program related to options and other programs.

Gillette "may or may not reinstitute a small buyback program in the next year or two that would be related to options and other share purchase plans...Other than that we have no plans for a share buyback," Zeien said.
Zeien made the comments on a call with institutional investors following the company's announcement last week it would acquire Duracell International Inc in a more than $7 billion stock transaction.
Zeien also said Kohlberg Kravis & Roberts & Co, a major Duracell shareholder, "will be given registration rights for a secondary offering."
Zeien also said there is no lockup agreement. After the deal, KKR will own 6.8 percent of Gillette.

During the call, Zeien announced that Charles Perrin, currently Duracell CEO, would be named executive vice president at Gillette in charge of the Duracell division. He will be reporting to Gillette President Michael Hawley.
